name: EWA World Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: The fed's own served title-history page runs a fully dated fifteen-reign chain from Scott Cummings's tournament win on 12 January 1998 to Mortis's Triple Threat win on 9 October 1999, each change carrying its own stipulation note (a No Holds Barred match, a Steel Cage Death Match, a Ladder Match, a Casket Match) and one stretch — 20 April to a re-run tournament in October 1999 — recorded on the page's own ledger as "Vacant... Federation closed," the belt itself briefly outliving what its own note calls the fed's end. Thirteen of the belt's own reigns are reified here, chaining the two founding/closing anchors through Erik Draven's nine own reigns (the fed's own most-decorated titleholder), Stevie Richards's and Shawn Copeland's own repeated exchanges, and SmirtDogg's own three; the remaining stretches (Kane, Ric Flair, Prodigy, Jeff Bunda, Justin Hicks, Thorne Richards, and The Golden One's own reigns) still ride the title's own served page rather than a separate reigns.json row, pending those wrestlers' own future minting.

name: EWA European Championship
epitaph: The fed's own served title-history page runs a dated lineage from KG's tournament win on 2 March 1998 to Lee Tenn's win on 31 March 1999, ending vacant at the fed's own close with no post-closure revival recorded (unlike the World Heavyweight and Hardcore titles, which both saw one further reign after the fed's own "closed" ledger note). Seven of the belt's own reigns are reified here, chaining the founding and closing anchors through Stevie Richards's, Shawn Copeland's, SmirtDogg's, Erik Draven's, and Haywood Jublome's own reigns; the remaining stretches (Alex Wright, Prodigy, Makaveli, Edge, The Prince, and others' own reigns) still ride the title's own served page, pending those wrestlers' own future minting.

name: EWA Hardcore Championship
epitaph: The fed's own served title-history page runs a dated lineage from E-'Nuff's Triple Threat Steel Cage Weapons match win on 16 January 1999 to Nukeman's Nuclear Hell Match win on 13 October 1999 — like the World Heavyweight title, the belt briefly outlives the fed's own "closed" ledger note (recorded vacant from 20 April 1999) via a late-October revival chain. A third reign, Vendetta's own Junkyard Brawl win between the two anchors, is now also reified; the remaining stretch (Raven's and Reaper's own reigns) still rides the title's own served page, pending those wrestlers' own future minting.

name: EWA Intercontinental Championship
epitaph: The fed's own served title-history page runs a dated lineage from The Pessimist's tournament win on 15 January 1998 to Jack Daniels's Triple Threat Ladder Match win on 25 September 1999, the belt briefly outliving the fed's own "closed" ledger note (recorded vacant from 20 April 1999) via a late-September revival. Seven of the belt's own reigns are reified here, chaining the founding and closing anchors through Scott Cummings's, Shawn Michaels's, Haywood Jublome's, Grady Smith's, and Venom's own reigns; the remaining stretches (Scott Hall, Hannibal Manson, Deathstar, Jeff Bunda, Crazy Canuck, Ruger Ice, The Rock, Terry Conklin, Jack Reed, and Tanaka's own reigns) still ride the title's own served page, pending those wrestlers' own future minting.

name: EWA Light Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: The fed's own served title-history page runs a dated lineage from SmirtDogg's tournament win on 12 January 1998 to The Kaze's six-man Four Corners win on 9 October 1999, the belt briefly outliving the fed's own "closed" ledger note (recorded vacant from 20 April 1999) via a late-1999 revival chain. Six of the belt's own reigns are reified here, chaining the founding and closing anchors through Shawn Michaels's, Shawn Copeland's, Philip Donovan's, and Lunatikk Crippler's own reigns; the remaining stretches (Aaron Martin's own several reigns, Thorne Richards, Joe Satre, New Jack, The Prince, Scott Tokage, Terry Conklin, Michael Modest, Max Pins, and Craven Blood's own reigns) still ride the title's own served page, pending those wrestlers' own future minting.

name: EWA Television Championship
epitaph: The fed's own served title-history page runs a dated lineage from Hunter Hearst Helmsley's tournament win on 2 February 1998 to Philip Donovan's Three Way Dance win on 22 September 1999, the belt briefly outliving the fed's own "closed" ledger note (recorded vacant from 20 April 1999) via a late-September revival. Seven of the belt's own reigns are reified here, chaining the founding and closing anchors through KG's two own reigns, Stevie Richards's, Venom's, and Hunter Hearst Helmsley's own second reign; the remaining stretches (Steve Austin, Eclipse, Castor Troy, The Gunslinger, and many others' own reigns) still ride the title's own served page, pending those wrestlers' own future minting.

name: EWA United States Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: The fed's own served title-history page runs a dated lineage from SmirtDogg's Battle Royal win on 15 January 1998 to Bret Hart's win on 13 October 1999, the belt briefly outliving the fed's own "closed" ledger note (recorded vacant from 20 April 1999) via a late-1999 revival chain; the same page's own notes record the title briefly renamed "North American" after a unification with a Canadian belt (note 8) and renamed back to United States when all EWA titles were declared vacant (note 15). Ten of the belt's own reigns are reified here, chaining the founding and closing anchors through Erik Draven's own four reigns, SmirtDogg's second, KG's, Stevie Richards's, Kanyon's, and "Cold" Harding Cash's own reigns; the remaining stretches (Prodigy, The Golden Child, Dallas Page, Raven, Justin Hicks, The Wyldsyde, Vic Deakins, and others' own reigns) still ride the title's own served page, pending those wrestlers' own future minting.

name: EWA World Tag Team Championship
epitaph: The fed's own served title-history page runs a dated lineage from Harlem Heat's tournament win on 12 January 1998 to Jack Daniels and Venom's win on 6 October 1999, the belts briefly outliving the fed's own "closed" ledger note (recorded vacant from 20 April 1999) via a late-1999 revival chain. Two reigns are reified here: Jack Daniels and Venom's own closing win, and Shawn Copeland and Erik Draven's own battle-royal win between two vacancies.
